text:
Good evening. It is Friday, October ninth.

First, the news from home.

Story one. In a widely discussed public policy decision reported by both Starr F M and Three News, the government has suspended its controversial ban on preaching and hawking inside moving commercial vehicles. The restriction under Legislative Instrument twenty-five nineteen had sparked intense public outcry and debate surrounding religious expression before officials decided to put the measure on hold.

Story two. Graphic Online reports that the pressure group OccupyGhana has issued a strong warning to the Economic and Organised Crime Office, the Bureau of National Investigation, and other investigative bodies. The group demanded that these agencies stop turning investigations into punishment, raising concerns about due process over the use of account freezes, agency-imposed bail, travel bans, and arrests.

Story three. Graphic Online also reports that the former National Chairman of the National Peace Council, Most Reverend Professor Emmanuel Asante, has urged that fundamental national interests must rise above partisan politics. He stressed that key priorities like education, health, and economic development should be pursued by all political parties devoid of extreme partisanship, even if they disagree on the exact means to achieve them.

Story four. On the party political front, MyJoyOnline reports that newly elected national executives of the New Patriotic Party, led by John Boadu, have met former President Kufuor and assured him of their commitment to strengthen internal unity. Meanwhile, The Ghana Report reveals that about eight hundred and thirty aspirants have picked nomination forms to contest various regional positions in the opposition National Democratic Congress Greater Accra elections.

Now, around the world.

Story five. According to reports from the B B C, Deutsche Welle, and Africanews, military tensions are escalating in the Horn of Africa as Ethiopia and Eritrea trade accusations of starting a conflict. Truckloads of Eritrean soldiers have reportedly driven across the border into Ethiopia, prompting reported Ethiopian drone strikes in Tigray and raising deep international fears of a wider regional war.

Story six. The B B C, The Guardian, and France twenty-four report that South African jurist and former United Nations human rights chief Navi Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. The Norwegian Nobel Committee honoured the eighty-five-year-old judge for her lifelong work promoting peace, human rights, and international law, including her investigations into crimes in Rwanda and the Palestinian territories.

You can open Dad News and ask for more about any story by saying its number.
